title: Marguerite and the Border
premise: Mara Fairweather, a disgraced intelligence analyst now freelancing on deniable cases, is hired to trace a passenger who never existed aboard Flight 447, whose records vanish mid-flight. Following the ghost through border towns and forged identities, Mara discovers the flight was a rehearsal for an attack designed to look like a catastrophic accident, orchestrated by the very agency that once discarded them. Torn between loyalty to a handler who may be the enemy and a stranger aboard the vanished plane who becomes their only ally, Mara races to expose the plot before a second, real 'accident' occurs. In the end Mara burns their own last credential to force the truth into daylight, choosing belonging with the living over inheritance from the institutions that made them.
about_author: Jonah Winterbourne is the pen name of a former logistics consultant who spent a decade shuttling between border cities and now writes thrillers about people caught between jurisdictions. They live off-grid in coastal Maine with two rescue dogs and a stubborn refusal to own a smartphone.

chapters.title: The Passenger Who Wasn't
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Broke and blacklisted after three agency dismissals, Mara takes a cash job: find out why a name on Flight 447's manifest disappears from every database while the plane is still airborne. The beat is weary competence masking hunger for redemption.

chapters.title: Forty Thousand Feet of Nothing
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Cross-checking radar archives, Mara finds a ninety-second gap where 447's transponder blinks out — then returns. The airline denies everything. The emotional beat is the first cold prickle of dread: someone with institutional power is scrubbing history in real time.

chapters.title: The Handler's Offer
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Former mentor Elias Vann reappears, offering reinstatement if Mara drops the case. He slips them a redacted file by 'mistake.' Mara can't tell if it's bait or a warning; the beat is the ache of old loyalty meeting new suspicion.

chapters.title: Ghost at Gate C
chapters.summary: Alternate POV: Ilsa Renner, the ghost passenger, alive and hiding in a border city hotel, watching news coverage of her own death. She carries a stolen drive she doesn't fully understand. Her beat is terror sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Paper Borders
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Tracing forged identity chains through corrupt document brokers, Mara learns the ghost's papers were minted inside a government print shop. The beat is vertigo — the conspiracy isn't hiding from the state; it is the state.

chapters.title: Two Strangers, One Room
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Mara and Ilsa collide in the hotel corridor, each mistaking the other for an assassin. A tense standoff becomes uneasy alliance when assassins actually arrive. The beat is adrenaline giving way to fragile trust between two people with nothing left to lose.

chapters.title: What the Drive Remembers
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. The drive contains flight-telemetry edits proving 447 was remotely rerouted as a dry run. Ilsa reveals she was a maintenance contractor who copied it on instinct. Her beat is guilt: she signed off on a component that will be used again.

chapters.title: The Accident Calendar
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Decoding maintenance schedules, Mara finds a pattern of past 'accidents' — all near borders, all politically convenient. The next window opens in eleven days. The beat is the clock starting, dread becoming arithmetic.

chapters.title: Vann's Confession, Almost
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara confronts Vann, who admits the program exists but claims he's playing double agent to stop it. He gives them a safehouse key. The beat is longing to believe him warring with every scar from his earlier betrayals.

chapters.title: Safehouse, Unsafe
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. The safehouse is compromised; Ilsa escapes through service tunnels while Mara covers her retreat, taking a bullet graze. The beat is sacrifice offered without hesitation — and Ilsa realizing Mara matters to her beyond the mission.

chapters.title: Inheritance of Lies
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Digging into the program's funding, Mara finds their own dismissal was engineered to make them deniable — they were always meant to be the fall guy. The beat is rage transmuted into clarity: this fight is personal by design.

chapters.title: The Border Town That Knew
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. In a dusty crossing town, a retired customs officer recognizes the attack profile: cargo planes, 'mechanical failure,' a valley full of refugees. His testimony humanizes the stakes. The beat is grief for the previous accidents no one investigated.

chapters.title: Eleven Becomes Six
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. A leak accelerates the timeline — the strike window moves up five days. Vann goes silent. The beat is panic managed into method as Mara and Ilsa plan to physically intercept the target aircraft's ground crew.

chapters.title: Hangar Nine
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Inside a private hangar, Ilsa plants a tracker on the rigged airframe but is recognized by the program's field chief, Calloway. She escapes barely. The beat is courage costing something: her face is now known.

chapters.title: The Trap Wearing a Friend's Face
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Vann resurfaces, begging Mara to stand down, claiming interception will trigger martial-law contingency. Mara realizes his 'confession' was scripted to steer them. The beat is heartbreak — cutting the last thread to the institution that raised them.

chapters.title: Counterfeit Sky
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Mara and Ilsa split: Mara feeds false telemetry to the remote hijack team while Ilsa reaches the tower. The deception half-works; the attack is delayed, not stopped. The beat is hope curdling under pressure.

chapters.title: Calloway's Ledger
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Captured briefly by Calloway, Mara talks instead of breaks, learning the endgame: blame the attack on a neighboring state to justify intervention. Released as a patsy-in-waiting. The beat is humiliation weaponized into defiance.

chapters.title: Ninety Seconds Again
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. The target flight departs with the same transponder gap as 447. Ilsa, aboard as a last-minute contractor, must reach the avionics bay while Mara talks her through it by hidden radio. The beat is claustrophobic intimacy — two voices against a falling sky.

chapters.title: Marguerite
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Ilsa reaches the bay; the override fails; Mara makes the call to broadcast the cockpit's distress and the telemetry proof simultaneously, forcing air-traffic systems worldwide to watch. The plane lands hard but lands. The beat is love declared in procedure and static.

chapters.title: The Fall Guys
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The agencies move to bury everything and pin it on Mara and Ilsa. But the worldwide broadcast created witnesses; a foreign aviation board demands the data. The beat is exhausted triumph knowing the machine will retaliate.

chapters.title: Testimony at the Border
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At a neutral-country hearing, Vann testifies truthfully at last, trading his career for theirs; Calloway is indicted abroad. The beat is justice arriving partial and late, and being worth it anyway.

chapters.title: Belonging
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, epilogue tone. Months later, Mara and Ilsa live quietly in the border town that helped them, running a small records-recovery nonprofit for the forgotten dead of past 'accidents.' The final beat is peace earned: home chosen, not inherited.
